changelog:
v5.3: arm correlation_taper (strength 1.5, onset_quantile 0.7, floor 0.3, 60d lookback) on the equity sleeve. Each holding is trimmed in proportion to its weighted-average correlation to the REST of the book — continuous, no threshold, the mechanism built in v5.x and left unarmed. Nine of ten axes improve: Martin 3.319->3.513, sCopley 1.787->1.916, cvar3m/6m/12m -7.30/-6.84/-3.17 -> -6.60/-6.20/-2.99, worst-3m/6m/12mo -14.12/-10.80/-7.71 -> -13.88/-9.61/-7.44, maxDD -15.31->-15.15%, RDD3y 3.36->2.98. Costs CAGR 13.04->12.64% (vs 60/40's 8.13%) and turnover 4.72->4.95. onset_quantile chosen at 0.7 as the point where NOTHING regresses: q0.5 gives a better quarter (sCopley 2.000) but rots worst-12mo to -8.35%, q0.8 gives a better year (-6.90%) but barely improves the quarter. Strength beyond 1.5 keeps lifting sCopley while worst-12mo decays behind it - an interior optimum, not a max. Refuted en route: event_triggers/portfolio_drawdown is actively HARMFUL (sCopley 1.787->1.430, worst-12mo -7.71->-13.34%) - it sells the bottom and misses the rebound, which kills the 'cadence not composition' thread in that form; per_fund_inverse_vol vol_scaling is mildly negative on nearly every axis.

[D6 regression accepted on longest underwater (d): Longest-relative-underwater-days vs 60/40 lengthens. Accepted because it is a TRACKING statistic and every ABSOLUTE pain measure improves together - all three CVaR horizons, all three worst-rolling windows, maxDD - and the other three D6 instruments pass, with RDD3y itself improving 3.36->2.98. A more diversified, lower-equity-beta book will spend longer stretches modestly behind a 60/40 blend during equity-led runs; that is the mechanism working, not a drawdown. Preserve's promise is worst-quarter smoothness, which is exactly what improved, and CAGR 12.64% still clears the 60/40 constraint at 8.13%.]
